preamble: Atypical Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  KDIGO 2021 / International Consensus Guidelines on aHUS (Goodship et al.) / ERA-EDTA Working Group  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Does the patient require renal replacement therapy (dialysis) at presentation, or has eGFR fallen below 15 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 5)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — dialysis-requiring AKI or CKD Stage 5 at nadir; worst renal severity tier; ESRD risk >60% without sustained eculizumab

questions.question: Is the platelet nadir <50,000/μL or is there CNS involvement (seizures, stroke, encephalopathy) at presentation?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe TMA with thrombocytopenia <50K or CNS injury confirmed; high morbidity and ESRD risk

questions.question: Was eculizumab initiated >7 days after TMA onset, or was complement blockade not started due to delayed diagnosis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — treatment delay confirmed; each additional day without eculizumab increases irreversible renal injury risk

questions.question: Is there a pathogenic variant in complement factor H (CFH)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — CFH mutation confirmed; highest ESRD risk among complement gene mutations (~70–80% ESRD without sustained treatment)

questions.question: Is there a pathogenic variant in complement C3 or complement factor B (CFB)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — C3 or CFB gain-of-function mutation confirmed; systemic complement activation; high relapse risk off eculizumab

questions.question: Is there a pathogenic variant in MCP/CD46 (membrane cofactor protein)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — MCP mutation confirmed; lower ESRD risk than CFH (~20–30%) but relapse risk elevated with intercurrent illness

questions.question: Did platelet count and LDH normalize within 2 weeks of eculizumab initiation (complete TMA response)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — complete TMA response confirmed; favorable short-term response but long-term renal recovery depends on chronicity

questions.question: Has the patient had ≥1 TMA relapse (recurrent MAHA + thrombocytopenia + AKI) while on or after stopping eculizumab?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — TMA relapse confirmed; lifelong eculizumab required; consider switch to ravulizumab (longer dosing interval)

questions.question: Has eculizumab been discontinued with subsequent TMA relapse, or is discontinuation being considered in a high-risk genotype?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high relapse risk with discontinuation confirmed; CFH mutations nearly universally relapse off treatment

questions.question: Is eGFR <45 mL/min/1.73m² (CKD Stage 3b or worse) after ≥3 months of sustained eculizumab therapy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — incomplete renal recovery confirmed; significant irreversible nephron loss from acute TMA episodes

questions.question: Is there significant thrombotic microangiopathy chronicity on renal biopsy (>25% tubular atrophy/interstitial fibrosis or arterial sclerosis)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — chronic TMA injury confirmed on histology; residual nephron loss limits long-term renal outcome

questions.question: Is there documented neurological injury from CNS TMA (cognitive impairment, seizure disorder, stroke sequelae) persisting after acute episode?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — persistent CNS TMA injury confirmed; extrarenal complement-mediated injury; indicates systemic TMA burden

questions.question: Is there cardiomyopathy or cardiac TMA confirmed (troponin elevation + wall motion abnormality) during or after aHUS episode?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — cardiac TMA involvement confirmed; rare but high-mortality complication; systemic complement blockade essential
